labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
When connecting to an MCP server via SSE transport, tools are successfully discovered and registered (confirmed by hermes tools list showing all N tools). The SSE connection appears healthy — the _servers dict is populated and the server object is present. However, tool calls intermittently fail with: MCP server 'playwright_win' is not connected

Steps to reproduce:
1. Configure an MCP server with transport: sse pointing to a Windows Playwright MCP server at http://<windows-ip>:8931/sse
2. Start the gateway — tools are discovered and registered successfully
3. Run any mcp_playwright_win_* tool (e.g., browser_navigate)
4. Tool call fails with the error above, despite playwright_win appearing in _servers

Expected behavior:
Tool calls should succeed when the server is connected and session is active.

Actual behavior:
MCP server 'playwright_win' is not connected
Session terminated

Environment:
- OS: WSL2 (Ubuntu) connecting to Windows host
- MCP Python package: 1.27.2
- MCP server: @playwright/mcp on Windows, SSE endpoint at http://172.23.160.1:8931/sse
- Direct Python test via sse_client → ClientSession → call_tool succeeds every time
- The failure only occurs when calling tools through the Hermes Gateway tool executor

Analysis:
The _servers dict is populated in a thread via run_in_executor(None, discover_mcp_tools), and tool calls read it with _lock held at mcp_tool.py:2324-2326. The server object exists in _servers (confirmed via gateway logs showing discovery complete, _servers now: ['playwright_win']), but server.session appears to be None at call time, or the server object itself is not found — despite the SSE session being active and usable in direct Python tests.

Possible root causes:
1. The _servers dict or server.session is being cleared/reset from a different code path after discovery but before tool execution
2. The tool executor accesses a different instance of the _servers dict than the one populated by discovery
3. The SSE session is closed by the server between the health-check path and the tool-call path

Logs:
# Gateway startup — discovery succeeds:
discovery complete, _servers now: ['playwright_win']  # 23 tools registered

# Tool call fails:
MCP server 'playwright_win' is not connected
Session terminated

Additional context:
- Direct sse_client test (Python, same parameters) works perfectly and repeatedly
- The Playwright MCP server on Windows is healthy and reachable at /sse
- No Missing session ID / 400 Bad Request errors — ruling out MCP GitHub Issue #20349

## Problem

`setup.py` unconditionally walks both `skills` and `optional-skills` during package metadata/build evaluation. If either directory is absent from an sdist, downstream source package, or minimal checkout, metadata generation/build can fail before setuptools can install the package.

Evidence:
- `setup.py:12-20` (`_data_file_tree`)
- `setup.py:23-27`

## Suggested fix

Make `_data_file_tree` tolerate missing roots by returning `[]` when the root does not exist, or otherwise ensure package metadata always includes those directories in every source distribution path.

## Suggested regression test

Add a packaging test that invokes `_data_file_tree` with a missing temporary root and asserts it returns `[]`, plus a source distribution build smoke if packaging tests exist.

The project pins runtime dependencies exactly, but isolated build environments can still resolve any future setuptools release because `[build-system].requires` uses `setuptools>=61.0` with no ceiling/exact pin. A breaking or compromised future setuptools release could affect installs before runtime dependency pins are considered.

Pin or upper-bound the build backend requirement consistently with the repo dependency policy, then update any lock/build metadata as needed.

## Suggested regression test

Add a packaging policy check that rejects unbounded requirements in `[build-system].requires`.

items.title: Bug: live model discovery silently replaces user-configured models in /model picker

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary

When the `/model` picker performs live `/models` discovery for a provider with valid credentials, it **replaces** the entire user-configured model list with the live response — silently dropping any models the user explicitly configured under `providers:` or `custom_providers:` with metadata overrides (e.g. `context_length`).

This is a data-loss bug in the picker UI: models the operator deliberately configured are invisible in the picker despite being correctly used at runtime.

## Affected paths

Both Section 3 (`providers:` dict) and Section 4 (`custom_providers:` list) in `hermes_cli/model_switch.py` are affected.

### Section 3 (`providers:`)

```python
# line ~1532 (main)
live_models = fetch_api_models(api_key, api_url)
if live_models:
    models_list = live_models  # ← replaces user-configured list
```

### Section 4 (`custom_providers:`)

```python
# line ~1726 (main)
live_models = fetch_api_models(api_key, api_url)
if live_models:
    grp["models"] = live_models          # ← replaces user-configured list
    grp["total_models"] = len(live_models)
```

## Reproduction

1. Configure a provider with explicit models that have metadata overrides:

```yaml
custom_providers:
  - name: Private Relay
    base_url: https://relay.example.internal/v1
    api_key: sk-relay-test
    models:
      configured-model:
        context_length: 200000
      manual-only-model:
        context_length: 128000
```

2. Ensure the endpoint `/v1/models` returns a different catalog (e.g. `["live-model-a", "live-model-b"]`).
3. Open the `/model` picker.
4. Observe: only `live-model-a` and `live-model-b` appear. `configured-model` and `manual-only-model` are gone.

## Expected behavior

Live-discovered models should be **merged** (deduplicated) with the user-configured list, not replace it. Models explicitly configured by the user should always appear in the picker — they may carry metadata (context_length, pricing, etc.) that the live `/models` endpoint does not provide.

## Actual behavior

User-configured models are silently discarded when live discovery succeeds.

## Suggested fix

Change assignment to deduplicated merge in both sections:

```python
# Section 3
live_models = fetch_api_models(api_key, api_url)
if live_models:
    for m in live_models:
        if m and m not in models_list:
            models_list.append(m)

# Section 4
live_models = fetch_api_models(api_key, api_url)
if live_models:
    for m in live_models:
        if m and m not in grp["models"]:
            grp["models"].append(m)
    grp["total_models"] = len(grp["models"])
```

Also filter empty model IDs from live `/models` responses for consistency.

## Related

- #8758 — custom_providers models mapping ignored by picker (overlapping symptom)
- #20582 — custom provider shows only one model (related discovery gap)
- #12977 — context_length override not propagated to auxiliary path (same class: user config silently dropped)
- #23609 — picker skips live fetch entirely for built-in api_key providers (upstream: once live fetch works, this replace bug activates)
- #30653 — key_env not resolved in Section 4 (prerequisite: without key_env fix, live fetch never runs, so this replace bug is masked)
- PR #35145 — proposed fix for this issue

items.body:
Hindsight Plugin (client v0.6.1) calls wrong API endpoint — incompatible with Hindsight Server v0.7.1
labels: ["bug", "memory", "hindsight"]
---

## 🐛 Bug Description

The `hindsight_retain` tool in Hermes Agent consistently fails with a timeout error. The integrated Hindsight Plugin (using `hindsight-client==0.6.1`) attempts to call the endpoint `/retain`, but a Hindsight Server running version `0.7.1` relocated this endpoint to `/v1/default/banks/{bank_id}/memories`.

**Error from agent.log:**
```
WARNING hindsight_retain returned error (120.00s): {"error": "Failed to store memory: "}
```

**Direct curl proof:**
```bash
# What Hermes calls → 404
curl -s -X POST "http://192.168.1.236:8888/retain" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"content":"Test","tags":["hermes-test"]}'
# → {"detail":"Not Found"}

# What the server (0.7.1) expects → should work
curl -s -X POST "http://192.168.1.236:8888/v1/default/banks/claus-default/memories" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"content":"Test","tags":["hermes"]}'
# → expected: success response
```

This means long-term memory storage (`hindsight_retain`) is **completely non-functional** with Hindsight Server v0.7.1, while recall and health checks work.

---

## 📋 Steps to Reproduce

1. Run Hermes Agent v0.15.1 with `memory.provider: hindsight` in `config.yaml`.
2. Point it at a Hindsight Server v0.7.1 on any host (e.g., `192.168.1.236:8888`).
3. Send any message that triggers an automatic `hindsight_retain` call.
4. Wait ~120 seconds → the tool call times out with `Failed to store memory`.
5. Check the log:
   ```bash
   grep hindsight_retain ~/.hermes/logs/agent.log
   ```

---

## ✅ Expected Behavior

`hindsight_retain` should successfully store a new memory in the Hindsight Server. The API endpoint called by the Hermes plugin must match the endpoint exposed by the running server version.

---

## ❌ Actual Behavior

The tool call fails after a 120-second timeout. Root cause: Hermes Plugin (client `0.6.1`) calls `POST /retain`, but Hindsight Server (`0.7.1`) exposes `POST /v1/default/banks/{bank_id}/memories`.

| Action | Hermes Plugin (client 0.6.1) | Hindsight Server (0.7.1) |
|--------|------------------------------|---------------------------|
| **retain** | `POST /retain` ❌ | `POST /v1/default/banks/{bank_id}/memories` ✅ |
| **recall** | `POST /recall` ❌ | `POST /v1/default/banks/{bank_id}/memories/recall` ✅ |

---

## 🔧 Affected Component

```
plugins/memory/hindsight/ (integrated Hermes plugin)
→ uses hindsight-client==0.6.1 (pip package in venv)
→ calls client.aretain() which uses the old flat endpoint /retain
```

---

## 🩺 Debug Report

```
version:          0.15.1 (2026.5.29) [b3aaf267]
os:               Linux 7.0.2-3-pve x86_64
python:           3.11.15
openai_sdk:       2.24.0
memory_provider:  hindsight
gateway:          running (systemd)
git HEAD:         b3aaf2676
```

---

## 💻 Operating System

```
Linux 7.0.2-3-pve (Proxmox PVE) x86_64
```

---

## 🐍 Python Version

```
Python 3.11.15
```

---

## 📦 Hermes Version

```
Hermes Agent v0.15.1 (2026.5.29) — Git: b3aaf2676
```

---

## 🔍 Root Cause Analysis

The `hindsight-client` pip package version `0.6.1` (shipped in Hermes venv) hardcodes the old, flat API path `/retain`. The Hindsight Server version `0.7.1` changed to a versioned path structure:

| Version | Retain Endpoint |
|---------|-----------------|
| v0.5.x / v0.6.x | `/retain` |
| v0.7.x (beta?) | `/v1/retain` |
| v0.7.1 (final) | `/v1/default/banks/{bank_id}/memories` |

**Relevant code paths in Hermes:**
- **Plugin entry point:** `/usr/local/lib/hermes-agent/plugins/memory/hindsight/__init__.py`
- **Plugin calls:** `client.aretain(**retain_kwargs)` at **line 1532**
- **Client definition:** `/usr/local/lib/hermes-agent/venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/hindsight_client/hindsight_client.py`
- **Client methods:** `retain()` at **line 250**, `retain_batch()` at **line 298**, `aretain()`, `aretain_batch()`

The underlying auto-generated OpenAPI client (`hindsight_client_api`) was generated from a Hindsight Server spec older than v0.7.1, so it still uses the old flat path.

**API Discovery:**
```bash
# Server health endpoint (works)
curl -s http://192.168.1.236:8888/health
# → {"status":"healthy","database":"connected"}

# OpenAPI spec (available on the server)
curl -s http://192.168.1.236:8888/openapi.json | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['info']['version'])"
# → "0.7.1"
```

---

## 🛠️ Proposed Fix

### Option A (Recommended — package update)

```bash
source /usr/local/lib/hermes-agent/venv/bin/activate
pip install --upgrade hindsight-client
```

If `hindsight-client >= 0.7.0` exists on PyPI, the new version should contain the updated auto-generated API client with the correct `/v1/...` paths. A simple `pip upgrade` would fix it without any code changes.

### Option B (Manual patch — fragile workaround)

Edit the auto-generated API client to replace old endpoint paths with new versioned ones:
```bash
# Location of auto-generated API
/usr/local/lib/hermes-agent/venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/hindsight_client_api/
```
This is fragile and not recommended for production.

### Option C (Downgrade server)

Pin the Hindsight Server to version `0.6.x` to match the existing client.

---

## 🤝 Are you willing to submit a PR?

- [ ] Yes, I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR
- [x] No (I'm not a developer, reporting for awareness)

items.title: [Bug]: Kanban dispatcher hangs forever on an unbounded fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX) in kanban_db.connect() under concurrent board access
items.body:
### Bug Description

Every kanban_db.connect() grabs a host-wide exclusive, unbounded file lock (fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_EX) in _cross_process_init_lock()) around its whole body — on every connect, not just first-open. Under concurrency, one process stalling inside that critical section makes the long-lived gateway dispatcher's next-tick connect() block forever (no timeout, no LOCK_NB). The gateway process stays alive, so Restart=on-failure never fires; the board silently stops being worked until a manual restart.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Gateway with embedded dispatcher (dispatch_in_gateway: true), one active board.
2. Put the board under concurrent load — many short-lived workers + a few external processes calling connect() (e.g. hermes kanban list in a loop / scripts), enough that the integrity-check-under-lock windows overlap.
3. Dispatcher logs reaped N zombie worker(s) then never logs its spawned=… summary; cards pile in todo, 0 running.
4. Process alive, no traceback, errors.log empty. Only a restart recovers it.

### Expected Behavior

a tick completes or fails with a bounded, logged error and re-ticks

### Actual Behavior

indefinite block inside connect() on flock(LOCK_EX)

### Affected Component

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Report     https://paste.rs/MlSNJ
agent.log  https://paste.rs/8tzjW
```

### Operating System

ubuntu 24.04.2

### Python Version

_No response_

### Hermes Version

_No response_

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

## Root cause

  ### The bug

  [`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:1128`](kanban_db.py#L1128) — `_cross_process_init_lock()` uses a bare blocking flock:

  ```python
  # kanban_db.py:1157
  fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)     # no LOCK_NB, no timeout — unbounded
  ```

  [`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:1358`](kanban_db.py#L1358) — `connect()` wraps its **entire body** in that lock on **every** call:

  ```python
  # kanban_db.py:1386
  with _cross_process_init_lock(path):
      _validate_sqlite_header(path)
      _guard_existing_db_is_healthy(path)         # runs PRAGMA integrity_check (line 1342)
      resolved = str(path.resolve())
      conn = _sqlite_connect(path)
      ...
  ```

  But the work inside is already cache-gated by `_INITIALIZED_PATHS` (`:1336` skips the integrity-check, `:1419` skips schema init) — so **after first-open the lock guards nothing, yet it's still acquired on every `connect()`**.

  ### Why it hangs forever (not just 120s)

  The dispatcher runs `dispatch_once` inside `asyncio.to_thread` with **no timeout/cancellation** — `gateway/run.py:5417-5425` docstring:

  > any in-flight `to_thread` returns on its own after the current `dispatch_once` call finishes.

  So if that thread blocks inside `connect()` on the flock, the tick awaits it indefinitely.

  (A SQLite `busy_timeout` would instead *raise* `database is locked` after 120s → caught + logged as `tick failed`; that line never appears, confirming the block is the flock, not SQLite-layer contention.)

  ### Why it's load-correlated

  Every short-lived worker / CLI invocation calls `connect()` with a **cold** `_INITIALIZED_PATHS`, so each runs a full `PRAGMA integrity_check` (`:1342`) **while holding the host-wide exclusive lock** — serializing the whole host on an O(DB-size) check. One slow holder ⇒ the
  dispatcher's next-tick `connect()` blocks behind it.

  ### Ruled out (verified)

  - **Not a crash** — process alive, no traceback.
  - **Not OOM** — RSS flat ~100–190 MB, no oom-kill.
  - **Not the zombie reap** — `reap_worker_zombies` uses `os.waitpid(-1, os.WNOHANG)` (`:4841`), which is non-blocking, and its log line prints *before* the hang.
  - **Not auto-decompose / aux-LLM** — never fires here.
  - **Not SQLite `busy_timeout`** — that would log `tick failed`, which never appears.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

1. Skip the flock on the steady-state hot path — when resolved in _INITIALIZED_PATHS, connect() only needs WAL + busy_timeout (which already serialize safely); the flock is only needed for genuine first-open init. (This is the one-line change I'm running as a local patch and it resolves it.)
2. Bound the flock where it is taken: LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB + a deadline (e.g. HERMES_KANBAN_INIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT), raising OperationalError on timeout so the tick logs tick failed and re-ticks instead of wedging.
3. Don't run PRAGMA integrity_check under the host-wide lock on every short-lived first-open (gate it / run only in the long-lived gateway).

items.title: [Bug]: WhatsApp LID sender silently dropped — alias resolver reads wrong session dir on modern platforms/ layout

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
### Bug Description

`expand_whatsapp_aliases()` in `gateway/whatsapp_identity.py` resolves WhatsApp LID↔phone aliases by reading the bridge's `lid-mapping-*.json` files, but it hardcodes the session directory as:

```python
session_dir = get_hermes_home() / "whatsapp" / "session"
```

The WhatsApp adapter (`gateway/platforms/whatsapp.py`) instead derives its session path — and launches the bridge with `--session <that path>` — via the consolidated-layout helper:

```python
get_hermes_dir("platforms/whatsapp/session", "whatsapp/session")
```

`get_hermes_dir(new, old)` returns the **old** path only if it already exists on disk, otherwise the **new** one. So on any install that doesn't have a legacy `~/.hermes/whatsapp/session` directory (i.e. the modern `platforms/` layout), the bridge writes its mapping files to `platforms/whatsapp/session` while the resolver looks in `whatsapp/session`, which is empty or nonexistent.

The resolver finds zero mappings, `expand_whatsapp_aliases` returns just the bare LID, the LID isn't in the allowlist, and the inbound message is **silently dropped**. The module docstring claims to be the "single source of truth … so the two paths can never drift apart" — but the two paths have drifted.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the gateway with WhatsApp on a fresh/modern install (no legacy `~/.hermes/whatsapp/session` directory), so the bridge writes mappings under `platforms/whatsapp/session`.
2. Have a sender whose messages arrive as a LID (`<digits>@lid`) with their phone number in the allowlist.
3. The bridge writes `lid-mapping-<lid>.json` → phone, but the resolver reads the wrong directory.
4. `expand_whatsapp_aliases("<lid>@lid")` returns only `{"<lid>"}`, the allowlist check misses, the message is dropped with no error surfaced to the user.

Minimal unit reproduction (no network):

```python
import json
from gateway.whatsapp_identity import expand_whatsapp_aliases

# bridge writes mappings under the modern platforms/ layout
mapping_dir = HERMES_HOME / "platforms" / "whatsapp" / "session"
mapping_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
(mapping_dir / "lid-mapping-999999999999999.json").write_text(
    json.dumps("15551234567@s.whatsapp.net"))

# resolver reads HERMES_HOME/whatsapp/session → empty
assert expand_whatsapp_aliases("999999999999999@lid") == {"999999999999999"}
# expected: {"999999999999999", "15551234567"}
```

### Expected Behavior

The resolver reads mapping files from the same directory the adapter writes them to, so a LID sender resolves to their phone alias and is matched against the allowlist on both the modern (`platforms/whatsapp/session`) and legacy (`whatsapp/session`) layouts.

### Actual Behavior

On the modern layout the resolver reads an empty/nonexistent directory, returns the bare LID, the allowlist check fails, and the message is silently dropped. Affects any WhatsApp install on the `platforms/` layout where the sender is surfaced as a LID.

### Affected Component

Messaging Gateway (platform adapters, session routing)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

WhatsApp

### Operating System

macOS 26.4 (Apple Silicon)

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

v0.15.1 (2026.5.29)

### Root Cause Analysis

`gateway/whatsapp_identity.py::expand_whatsapp_aliases()` resolves the session directory independently of the adapter:

- Resolver: `get_hermes_home() / "whatsapp" / "session"` (hardcoded legacy path).
- Adapter (`gateway/platforms/whatsapp.py`, the bridge's actual write target): `get_hermes_dir("platforms/whatsapp/session", "whatsapp/session")`.

`get_hermes_dir` prefers the new consolidated path when the legacy directory is absent, so the two diverge on modern installs. The fix is to route the resolver through the same `get_hermes_dir(...)` call so it can never drift from the adapter on either layout.

items.body:
## Summary

`tests/hermes_cli/test_gui_command.py` has two darwin tests that fail with `StopIteration` on current `main`. PR #36198 (`79f7e7a1e`, "fix(desktop): make locally-built macOS app relaunchable after in-place self-update") added `_desktop_macos_relaunchable_fixup()` to `hermes_cli/main.py` `cmd_gui`, but did not update the gui command tests.

## Affected tests

- `test_gui_installs_packages_and_launches_desktop_app`
- `test_gui_forwards_desktop_environment_overrides`

## Root cause

`_desktop_macos_relaunchable_fixup()` runs between the pack build and the launch. On darwin, with a resolvable `codesign`, it fires two extra `subprocess.run` calls:

```python
subprocess.run(["xattr", "-cr", str(app)], check=False)
subprocess.run([codesign, "--force", "--deep", "--sign", "-", str(app)], check=False)
```

Both failing tests force `sys.platform = "darwin"` (via the `_make_packaged_executable` helper) and patch `shutil.which` to return a truthy path, so `codesign` resolves and the fixup executes. But each test supplies only two `subprocess.run` side effects:

```python
patch("hermes_cli.main.subprocess.run", side_effect=[pack_ok, launch_ok])
```

Call order is now: pack (consumes `pack_ok`) → fixup `xattr` (consumes `launch_ok`) → fixup `codesign` (`StopIteration`, swallowed by the fixup's `except`, prints `macOS relaunch fixup skipped:` with an empty reason) → launch (`StopIteration`, uncaught → test fails).

The other gui tests pass because they don't force darwin (source-mode test) or use `which=None` / `return_value` (skip-build tests).

## Reproduce

```
python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_gui_command.py -q
# 2 failed, 6 passed — StopIteration in unittest/mock.py _execute_mock_call
```

(Runs on Linux too; the tests monkeypatch the platform to darwin.)

## Suggested fix

Mock the fixup helper in the two darwin tests, matching how the same tests already mock the install helper `_run_npm_install_deterministic` (helper-level, not its internal subprocess calls):

```python
patch("hermes_cli.main._desktop_macos_relaunchable_fixup"),
```

Alternatively, extend the `side_effect` lists with `xattr`/`codesign` results and shift the launch-call assertion indices. Mocking the helper keeps the gui-command tests focused on orchestration (install → pack → launch).

## Problem

In long-running Hermes gateway sessions, LSP language-server processes (pyright, gopls, etc.) accumulate indefinitely and are never cleaned up, eventually exhausting the process file-descriptor limit.

## Root Cause

`LSPService` in `agent/lsp/manager.py` defines `DEFAULT_IDLE_TIMEOUT = 600` and tracks `_last_used` timestamps per `(server_id, workspace_root)` key — but **no background task ever checks these timestamps or reaps idle clients**.

Each unique `(server_id, workspace_root)` pair spawns a new language-server subprocess. In a gateway running for days/weeks, different session workspaces accumulate dozens of orphaned pyright processes.

## Impact

- File descriptor exhaustion (ulimit -n 256 hit after ~60 pyright processes)
- Cascading failures: WeChat delivery, proxy, SQLite all fail
- Silent degradation until limit is hit

## Expected Behaviour

Language-server clients idle past `idle_timeout` (default 600s) should be automatically shut down.

## Proposed Fix

Add an idle-reaper background task to `LSPService` that periodically checks `_last_used` and shuts down idle clients. PR follows.

items.title: Subagent delegation is a black box — zero visibility into child agent reasoning and tool calls

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## The Problem

When you spawn subagents via `delegate_task`, you see nothing while they run. No tool calls, no reasoning, no progress. Just a spinner and a wait.

A subagent taking 12 minutes on a legitimate deep task vs a subagent stuck in an infinite loop look identical. The user has no way to distinguish "still working" from "burning tokens in circles."

Every other agent platform (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI) streams subagent activity. Hermes gives silence.

## Source Code Investigation

`tools/delegate_tool.py` has the infrastructure already built:

- `DelegateEvent` types at line 526-543: `TASK_THINKING`, `TASK_TOOL_STARTED`, `TASK_TOOL_COMPLETED`, `TASK_PROGRESS`
- `_build_child_progress_callback()` at line 681-850 builds per-subagent callbacks capable of tree-view output

The CLI parent wires the callback correctly:
- `cli.py:5112` passes `tool_progress_callback=self._on_tool_progress`
- `agent/tool_executor.py:779` sets `agent._delegate_spinner`
- `tools/delegate_tool.py:1133` passes `tool_progress_callback=child_progress_cb` into every child AIAgent

## Where It Breaks

1. **`tool.completed` is intentionally dropped** (line 800-801) — only `tool.started` events produce output
2. **`subagent.complete` has no spinner output** (line 772) — only gateway relay, CLI users see nothing
3. **No delegation-specific progress config** — `display.tool_progress` controls all visibility, no granularity
4. **Spinner gate may not fire in CLI** — `_should_emit_quiet_tool_messages()` at `run_agent.py:720` returns True only when `tool_progress_callback is None`, but CLI always sets it

## Real-World Impact

Debugging a broken delegation config (provider set to `holographic` — a memory backend, not an LLM) took hours. Each failing call looked identical to a working one. With visibility: "Subagent 1: resolving provider holographic → FAILED" would have appeared in 30 seconds.

## Proposed Changes

1. Enable tree-view output by default on CLI — the code is written, the spinner gate needs to fire reliably
2. Stop dropping `tool.completed` — show what finished, not just what started
3. Show `subagent.complete` on CLI spinner — not just gateway relay

items.title: Telegram gateway auto-replies force MP3 for Opus-capable TTS providers
items.body:
## Summary

Telegram voice replies generated through `GatewayRunner._send_voice_reply()` always pass an explicit `.mp3` temporary path to `text_to_speech_tool()`. That bypasses the tool's Telegram-aware default `.ogg` path selection.

As a result, providers that can produce Opus/OGG directly are forced down their MP3 path for gateway auto-replies. ElevenLabs is affected today, and MiniMax `t2a_v2` can also emit Opus directly when requested.

## Root cause

`text_to_speech_tool()` selects `.ogg` for Telegram only when `output_path` is omitted. The gateway auto-reply path always supplies a filename such as:

```python
tts_reply_<uuid>.mp3
```

ElevenLabs then requests `mp3_44100_128` instead of `opus_48000_64`. MiniMax `t2a_v2` also hardcodes `audio_setting.format: "mp3"` even when an OGG path is appropriate.

## Expected behavior

For Telegram sessions:

- rewrite gateway-supplied `.mp3` temp destinations to `.ogg` when the selected built-in provider supports Opus output;
- request native Opus from ElevenLabs and MiniMax `t2a_v2`;
- preserve MP3 plus ffmpeg conversion for Edge TTS, xAI, legacy MiniMax endpoints, and other providers without direct Opus output;
- avoid overriding explicitly requested non-MP3 output formats.

## Proposed fix

Add a small provider capability resolver in `tools/tts_tool.py`, use it for Telegram output-path selection, and make MiniMax `t2a_v2` choose `opus` when the output path ends in `.ogg`.

Regression tests should cover gateway-style explicit `.mp3` paths for ElevenLabs and MiniMax.

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

When using `provider=bedrock` with a Claude model (`api_mode=anthropic_messages`),
the stale-stream watchdog occasionally triggers `_replace_primary_openai_client(reason="stale_stream_pool_cleanup")`,
which fails with a misleading warning:

```
WARNING run_agent: Failed to rebuild shared OpenAI client (stale_stream_pool_cleanup)
  thread=asyncio_0:... provider=bedrock
  base_url=https://bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
  model=us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7
  error=The api_key client option must be set either by passing api_key to the
        client or by setting the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable
```

The warning suggests an OpenAI credential is missing, which has nothing to do
with a Bedrock setup. The conversation is **not actually broken** — the rebuild
attempt is dead-code on this path and the next API request succeeds — but the
log is confusing and noisy.

## Reproduction

Bedrock + Claude streaming request that goes ≥180s without receiving a chunk.
In my logs this fires roughly when `bedrock-runtime.us-east-1` has a slow first
chunk; e.g. one occurrence at `2026-06-01 10:25:41`:

```
2026-06-01 10:25:41,099 WARNING agent.chat_completion_helpers: Stream stale for 180s
  (threshold 180s) — no chunks received.
  model=us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7 context=~35,790 tokens. Killing connection.
2026-06-01 10:25:41,279 WARNING run_agent: Failed to rebuild shared OpenAI client
  (stale_stream_pool_cleanup) ...
  error=The api_key client option must be set ...
2026-06-01 10:26:25,641 INFO  agent.conversation_loop: API call #4: model=us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7
  provider=bedrock in=50818 out=3686 total=54504 latency=224.6s
```

The turn completed normally (`API call #4` succeeded after the watchdog killed
the stalled stream). Same pattern observed on `2026-05-27 09:32` and
`2026-05-16 00:57`, all bedrock + claude-opus-4-7 + us-east-1.

## Root cause (as best I can tell)

In `agent/agent_init.py`, the bedrock + Claude path explicitly initialises:

- `agent.api_mode = "anthropic_messages"`
- `agent._anthropic_client = build_anthropic_bedrock_client(region)` (the real
  request client)
- `agent.client = None`
- `agent._client_kwargs = {}`

All actual requests on this path flow through `agent._anthropic_client`.
`agent.client` is intentionally `None`.

When the stale-stream watchdog in `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py` calls
`agent._replace_primary_openai_client(reason="stale_stream_pool_cleanup")`,
that helper unconditionally calls `create_openai_client(agent, self._client_kwargs, ...)`.
For `api_mode == "anthropic_messages"`, `_client_kwargs == {}`, and the function
falls through to the generic `OpenAI(**client_kwargs)` constructor — which is
where the `OPENAI_API_KEY` error originates.

The `_replace_primary_openai_client` call itself is harmless (the next request
uses `_anthropic_client`, not `agent.client`), but it generates a misleading
warning every time the stale-stream watchdog or any other rebuild trigger fires.

The other rebuild triggers — `stale_stream_pool_cleanup`,
`<provider>_credential_refresh`, `nous_credential_refresh`,
`copilot_credential_refresh`, `credential_rotation`, `dead_connection_cleanup`,
`fallback_timeout_apply`, and `recreate_closed:*` — all share this issue when
running under `anthropic_messages`.

## Suggested fix

Short-circuit at `_replace_primary_openai_client` when
`agent.api_mode == "anthropic_messages"`: return `True` (no-op success)
without invoking the OpenAI factory at all. Conceptually, "rebuild the shared
OpenAI client" doesn't apply on this provider — there is no OpenAI client to
rebuild; the real request client is `agent._anthropic_client` and rotates
through its own path. The early return covers all six rebuild call-sites in one
place (`stale_stream_pool_cleanup`, `<provider>_credential_refresh`,
`nous_credential_refresh`, `copilot_credential_refresh`, `credential_rotation`,
`dead_connection_cleanup`, `fallback_timeout_apply`, and `recreate_closed:*`)
without touching the lower-level factory.

I'll send a PR shortly. Two design choices I'll make there, happy to revisit
based on review:

- Short-circuit at `_replace_primary_openai_client` (the rebuild entrypoint)
  rather than at `create_openai_client` (the factory). The factory's existing
  per-provider early branches (`copilot-acp`, `google-gemini-cli`, `gemini`)
  return adapter clients; `anthropic_messages` has no client to return, so the
  semantically clean place to short-circuit is one layer up where the caller
  decides whether a rebuild is needed at all. This also leaves the factory's
  contract ("return a non-None client") intact.
- Log at `info` level (`"rebuild skipped for anthropic_messages api_mode"`)
  rather than silently short-circuiting, so the no-op is observable.

Thanks!

items.body:
## Problem

Currently, `allowed_chats` only filters group/channel messages — **DMs are never filtered** (as documented in the code). This means even with `allowed_chats` set, any user can message the bot in a private chat and get a response.

For security-conscious deployments where the bot has access to sensitive tools (Redmine, terminal, file system, etc.), there's no way to restrict access to specific authorized users.

## Proposed Solution

Add two new config options under `telegram:` (and other platform sections):

1. **`allowed_users`** — A comma-separated list of user IDs that are authorized to interact with the bot
   - When set, only messages from these user IDs are processed
   - All other users (in DMs or groups) are rejected
   - Empty/unset = no restriction (backward compatible)

2. **`unauthorized_message`** — Optional custom message to send to unauthorized users before ignoring them
   - If set, send this message once to the unauthorized user, then ignore all future messages
   - If unset, silently ignore (current behavior)

## Example Config

```yaml
telegram:
  reactions: false
  allowed_users: '830003638,123456789'
  unauthorized_message: '🚫 This bot is private. Unauthorized access is not permitted.'
```

## Use Case

- Single-user deployments where the bot should only respond to the owner
- Team deployments where only specific team members should have access
- Preventing abuse/leakage of sensitive integrations

## Current Workaround

None — DMs cannot be restricted at all with current `allowed_chats` implementation.

## Related Code

In `gateway/platforms/telegram.py`, the `_telegram_allowed_chats()` method explicitly states in its docstring:
> "DMs are never filtered."

The authorization check at line ~4898 only filters group chats:
```python
allowed = self._telegram_allowed_chats()
if allowed and chat_id_str not in allowed:
    return guest_mention  # Only applies to groups
```

When Hindsight is configured with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` (set in `~/.hermes/.env` by default) but the local model cache is missing (e.g. first run after install, or cache cleared), the daemon hangs during model initialization with no error, no timeout, and no feedback.

- The "thinking" state should be distinguishable from actual model inference

items.title: Bug: Context compression triggers repeatedly after fresh compress — last_prompt_tokens=-1 not updated until next API call

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Problem

After context compression completes, the HUD shows `-1/262.1K` (negative tokens). Immediately after, a new user message triggers a **second compression** before any API call has returned real token data. The display then jumps to `121.5K/262.1K`, cmp2 → cmp3.

**Expected**: After compression, `last_prompt_tokens` reflects the compressed size. A new message should NOT trigger another compression until the user actually adds enough tokens to exceed the threshold.

## Reproduction

1. Run a long session until context compression fires (threshold ~50%).
2. Compression completes → HUD shows `-1/262.1K, cmp1`.
3. Immediately send a new message (e.g., ask a question).
4. Observe: compression triggers again → `cmp2` (or `cmp3`).
5. Eventually API returns real token count → display shows `121.5K/262.1K`.

The extra compression is wasteful and confuses the user.

## Root Cause

`conversation_loop.py` line 3907:

```python
elif _compressor.last_prompt_tokens == -1:
    # Compression just ran and no API-reported prompt count
    # has arrived yet. Avoid treating a schema-heavy rough
    # post-compression estimate as real context pressure.
    _real_tokens = 0
```

The `-1` sentinel is meant as a temporary flag to skip compression until real API data arrives. However:

1. `tui_gateway/server.py:1423` reads `last_prompt_tokens` directly for HUD display:
   ```python
   ctx_used = getattr(comp, 'last_prompt_tokens', 0) or usage['total'] or 0
   ```
   Python's `-1 or ... ` returns `-1` (truthy), so the HUD shows `-1/262K`.

2. More critically, the second compression happens because `should_compress()` and the \*_real_tokens` check are separate paths. When `last_prompt_tokens == -1` and the user sends a new message, the rough estimate path can still trigger compression if the message history is large enough.

3. `last_prompt_tokens = -1` is set after compression but never restored to the actual compressed token count. It waits for the next API response's `prompt_tokens` field — but that doesn't arrive until the API call completes.

## Suggested Fix

After compression, estimate and set `last_prompt_tokens` to the compressed messages' token count:

```python
# After _compress_context() in conversation_loop.py
_messages = agent._compress_context(...)
# Set last_prompt_tokens to a rough estimate of the compressed context
compressor.last_prompt_tokens = estimate_request_tokens_rough(_messages, tools=agent.tools or None)
```

Alternatively, change the HUD display to clamp negative values:

```python
ctx_used = max(0, getattr(comp, 'last_prompt_tokens', 0) or usage['total'] or 0)
```

But the core fix should be updating `last_prompt_tokens` after compression rather than leaving it at `-1`.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v2026.5.29 (commit 79f7e7a1e)
- Model: Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 via SGLang (192.168.14.32:8000)
- macOS 26.5, TUI mode

items.body:
## Bug: Profile-level `disabled_toolsets` not applied in WebUI

**Severity:** Medium

### The Bug
When a Hermes profile defines `agent.disabled_toolsets` in its `config.yaml`
(e.g. `~/.hermes/profiles/pm/config.yaml`), the WebUI gateway ignores
it — tools that should be blocked are available anyway. The TUI/CLI is
unaffected.

### Root Cause
`gateway/run.py::_load_gateway_config()` loads only the global
`~/.hermes/config.yaml` (which has `disabled_toolsets: []`) and never
merges the profile-level config from
`~/.hermes/profiles/<profile>/config.yaml`.

### Affected Code
- `gateway/run.py:1411-1437` — `_load_gateway_config()` loads
  `~/.hermes/config.yaml` only
- `gateway/run.py:11784-11785` — reads `disabled_toolsets` from that
  non-merged config

### Contrast: TUI/CLI Works
`hermes_cli/main.py:216` `_apply_profile_override()` sets `HERMES_HOME`
to the profile directory before imports, so the config loader naturally
picks up the profile's `disabled_toolsets`.

### Fix Suggestion
Merge profile-level `agent.disabled_toolsets` on top of the global config
in the WebUI gateway's `_load_gateway_config()` (or at the point where
`disabled_toolsets` is read at line 11784-11785).

### Related Issues
- #33924 — related `disabled_toolsets` + gateway bug (different root cause)
- #25752 — cron bypasses `disabled_toolsets` (closed/fixed)

items.title: Image generation tool drops source images for OpenAI/Codex image edits
items.body:
## Summary

Hermes' OpenAI/Codex image generation integration can call `gpt-image-2`, but the agent-facing `image_generate` tool does not expose a source-image parameter and the plugin dispatch path does not forward one. This makes existing-image workflows such as photo restoration/upscaling impossible through the native OpenAI/Codex image route, even when that configured backend supports image input.

The visible failure mode is that Hermes can receive/analyze an uploaded image, but cannot pass that same image into the OpenAI/Codex image provider. The agent then tends to fall back to weaker deterministic edits, local upscalers, ComfyUI, or other workarounds, and may incorrectly tell the user that native/subscription image editing is unavailable.

## Why this looks like a bug

This is not just a missing prompt or user workflow issue. It is a provider/tool integration gap:

- The configured provider can support source-image edits through the OpenAI Responses API (`input_image`).
- The public Hermes tool schema only allowed text-to-image fields.
- The provider dispatch layer dropped any source-image intent before it could reach the plugin.
- The OpenAI/Codex plugin payload builder only emitted `input_text`, never `input_image`.

So a real provider capability was unreachable from the agent tool layer.

## Environment where observed

- Repo: `NousResearch/hermes-agent`
- Local checkout commit tested from: `2d5dcfabc`
- Hermes package version observed: `0.14.0`
- OS: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic
- Entry point: Telegram gateway / agent tool call
- Image provider: `openai-codex`
- Image model used in validation: `gpt-image-2-medium`

## Reproduction path

1. Configure Hermes image generation to use the OpenAI/Codex image provider.
2. Provide an existing image to Hermes, e.g. in Telegram.
3. Ask for a conservative source-preserving edit/restoration/upscale, e.g.:
   > Restore and upscale this photo. Keep the same person, crop, expression, lighting, and composition. Reduce JPEG/blocky pixelation without stylizing or inventing details.
4. The agent can inspect the uploaded image, but when it reaches `image_generate`, the exposed schema has no way to pass the source image.
5. The OpenAI/Codex image plugin receives a text-only request, so `gpt-image-2` is used as text-to-image instead of image-to-image/editing.

## Expected behavior

`image_generate` should accept an optional source image parameter when the configured backend supports it, for example:

```python
image_generate(
    prompt="Restore and upscale this photo while preserving identity and composition.",
    aspect_ratio="square",
    image_url="/path/to/source.jpg",
)
```

The OpenAI/Codex provider should convert that into a Responses API input containing both:

```json
{
  "type": "input_text",
  "text": "..."
}
```

and:

```json
{
  "type": "input_image",
  "image_url": "..."
}
```

Supported source forms should include at least:

- `http://...`
- `https://...`
- `data:...`
- local file paths, embedded as base64 data URLs

## Actual behavior before local fix

The relevant path was text-only:

- `tools/image_generation_tool.py`
  - Schema exposed `prompt` and `aspect_ratio`, but no `image_url` / `image_path`.
  - Handler did not read a source-image parameter.
  - Plugin dispatch did not forward a source-image argument.

- `plugins/image_gen/openai-codex/__init__.py`
  - `_build_responses_payload(...)` always built only an `input_text` item.
  - No helper existed to serialize remote/data/local images as `input_image`.

## User-visible impact

For photo restoration or image-editing requests, Hermes may:

- fail to use the configured native/subscription image backend,
- incorrectly imply that image editing is unavailable,
- fall back to ComfyUI/local tooling despite the user expecting OpenAI/Codex image editing,
- produce weaker or less faithful restoration results because the source image never reaches the image model.

This is especially noticeable for "same image, clearer" workflows, where text-to-image generation is the wrong operation.

## Local fix validated

I tested a local fix that adds optional source-image plumbing end-to-end:

- `tools/image_generation_tool.py`
  - Adds optional `image_url` to the tool schema.
  - Reads `image_url` / `image_path` in `_handle_image_generate(...)`.
  - Forwards `image_url` through `_dispatch_to_plugin_provider(...)`.

- `plugins/image_gen/openai-codex/__init__.py`
  - Adds source-image payload support.
  - Accepts remote URLs, data URLs, and local paths.
  - Embeds local files as base64 data URLs.
  - Includes optional `input_image` alongside `input_text` in the Responses payload.
  - Returns metadata indicating whether a source image was supplied.

- Tests added/updated:
  - `tests/tools/test_image_generation.py`
  - `tests/tools/test_image_generation_plugin_dispatch.py`
  - `tests/tools/test_openai_codex_image_gen_edit.py`

Validation command:

```bash
python -m pytest \
  tests/tools/test_image_generation.py \
  tests/tools/test_image_generation_plugin_dispatch.py \
  tests/tools/test_openai_codex_image_gen_edit.py \
  -q -o 'addopts='
```

Result:

```text
61 passed in 2.22s
```

Manual provider-level validation also succeeded with a local source image and returned:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "provider": "openai-codex",
  "model": "gpt-image-2-medium",
  "source_image": true
}
```

## Suggested fix direction

Add optional source-image support to the generic image tool and forward it only as an optional parameter. Providers that do not support image-to-image can ignore it or return a clear unsupported-capability error. Providers that do support it should serialize it into the provider-native image input format.

Suggested PR title:

```text
fix(image-gen): pass source images through OpenAI/Codex image provider
```

## Compatibility / risk notes

- Existing text-to-image calls remain unchanged if `image_url` is omitted.
- The new parameter is additive and optional.
- Local file embedding should validate file existence and use MIME detection/fallback carefully.
- Providers that do not support source images should fail explicitly rather than silently dropping the image.

items.body:
title: "[Bug]: v0.15.2 wheel missing hermes_cli/dashboard_auth — dashboard crashes on startup"
labels: ["bug"]
---

## Bug Description

The v0.15.2 PyPI wheel (`hermes_agent-0.15.2-py3-none-any.whl`, sha256 `1a062a38...`) is missing the `hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/` Python module. The source tag `v2026.5.29.2` contains this module (12 files), and a local `pip wheel` build from the same source correctly includes it (11 files). The result is that `hermes dashboard` crashes on startup with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hermes_cli.dashboard_auth'`.

The wheel does include a *plugin* version of `dashboard_auth` at `plugins/dashboard_auth/nous/` — but the Python module `hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/` imported by `web_server.py` is absent.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Hermes Agent v0.15.2 from PyPI:
   ```
   pip install hermes-agent==0.15.2
   ```
2. Start the dashboard:
   ```
   hermes dashboard --no-open
   ```
3. Error immediately appears:
   ```
   Traceback (most recent call last):
     File ".../hermes_cli/main.py", line 10937, in cmd_dashboard
       from hermes_cli.web_server import start_server
     File ".../hermes_cli/web_server.py", line 4822, in <module>
       from hermes_cli.dashboard_auth.routes import router as _dashboard_auth_router
   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hermes_cli.dashboard_auth'
   ```

## Expected Behavior

`hermes dashboard` should start without errors. The `hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/` module should be included in the wheel, just as it exists in the `v2026.5.29.2` source tag.

## Actual Behavior

Dashboard crashes on startup. The wheel's RECORD contains **0** entries for `hermes_cli/dashboard`, but **3** entries for the unrelated `plugins/dashboard_auth/nous/`.

Cross-check:
- `git archive v2026.5.29.2 hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/ | tar -t | wc -l` → **12 files** (source tag has it)
- `pip wheel` from source checkout → **11 files** under `hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/` in wheel
- Official PyPI wheel (`hermes_agent-0.15.2-py3-none-any.whl`) → **0 files** under `hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/`

## Affected Component

- Setup / Installation
- Other (Dashboard)

## Messaging Platform

- N/A (CLI only)

## Debug Report

(`hermes debug share` output available on request — system info is provided below instead)

## Operating System

- WSL2 (Windows Subsystem for Linux) on Windows 11
- Linux kernel: 6.6.114.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2
- Host: Ubuntu/Debian based

## Python Version

- System: 3.12.3
- Hermes venv: 3.11.15

## Hermes Version

- Hermes Agent v0.15.2 (2026.5.29.2)
- OpenAI SDK: 2.24.0

## Additional Logs / Traceback

Full traceback from `hermes dashboard`:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "hermes", line 6, in <module>
    sys.exit(main())
  File "hermes_cli/main.py", line 14303, in main
    args.func(args)
  File "hermes_cli/main.py", line 10937, in cmd_dashboard
    from hermes_cli.web_server import start_server
  File "hermes_cli/web_server.py", line 4822, in <module>
    from hermes_cli.dashboard_auth.routes import router as _dashboard_auth_router
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hermes_cli.dashboard_auth'
```

## Root Cause Analysis

The `hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/` module exists in the `v2026.5.29.2` git tag (verified with `git ls-tree` and `git archive`). The `setuptools` configuration in `pyproject.toml` includes `hermes_cli.*` in its `packages.find.include`, and a local `pip wheel` build correctly picks it up.

However, the official PyPI wheel (`sha256: 1a062a3813de8998021a290abaf18489a5c009717b1569855b617ff2caef4b76`) does not include this module. Only the Hermes plugin variant at `plugins/dashboard_auth/nous/` made it into the wheel.

This suggests the CI/build process for v0.15.2 may have built the wheel from a tree where `hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/` was not yet present, or from a slightly different commit than the tag. The v0.15.2 release was a hotfix (tag `v2026.5.29.2`) that only touched 5 files related to plugin.yaml packaging — it's possible the build workflow for this hotfix branched from a commit that predated the `dashboard_auth` module addition to `main`.

Possible causes:
1. CI built the wheel from a merge base that didn't include `dashboard_auth`
2. CI used a different `setuptools`/build configuration than a local `pip wheel`
3. The hotfix release branch was cut before `dashboard_auth` was added to `main`

## Proposed Fix

**Workaround** (immediate): Copy `hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/` from a source checkout:
```bash
cp -r /path/to/hermes-agent/hermes_cli/dashboard_auth <venv>/lib/python3.11/site-packages/hermes_cli/dashboard_auth
```

**Proper fix**: Rebuild the v0.15.2 wheel with all modules from the `v2026.5.29.2` tag included in the `packages.find` scope, and publish v0.15.3 or a new wheel.

The simplest CI fix would be to run a pre-publish sanity check:
```python
from setuptools import find_packages
pkgs = find_packages(include=['hermes_cli', 'hermes_cli.*'])
assert 'hermes_cli.dashboard_auth' in pkgs, "dashboard_auth module missing from wheel"
```

## Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

---
*Note: I am a Hermes Agent user who discovered this while upgrading from v0.14.0 to v0.15.2. The issue was initially confused with a restart/process-cache problem because the old dashboard process (v0.14.0) masked the error. The actual module-not-found error only appeared after killing the old process.*

items.title: feat(skills): 公式 skill 7種を採用 (powerpoint/nano-pdf/ocr/maps/arxiv/blogwatcher/youtube) — 公式フォルダ構成を完全一致で維持
items.body:
## 目的

公式 hermes-agent の即戦力 skill 7 種を GJ で使えるようにする。
**設計原則: 公式 GitHub の フォルダ構成を完全一致で維持する (改変・flatten・fork 禁止)。**

採用 skill:
| skill | 公式パス | 用途 |
|-------|---------|------|
| powerpoint | `skills/productivity/powerpoint/` | .pptx 作成・編集 (提案資料) |
| nano-pdf | `skills/productivity/nano-pdf/` | PDF テキスト/誤字修正 |
| ocr-and-documents | `skills/productivity/ocr-and-documents/` | PDF/スキャン文字抽出 |
| maps | `skills/productivity/maps/` | ジオコーディング/経路/POI |
| arxiv | `skills/research/arxiv/` | 論文検索 |
| blogwatcher | `skills/research/blogwatcher/` | ブログ/RSS 監視 |
| youtube-content | `skills/media/youtube-content/` | YouTube 字幕→要約 |

---

## ★ 最重要原則: 公式フォルダ構成を完全一致

```
公式 (NousResearch/hermes-agent):
  skills/
    productivity/powerpoint/SKILL.md + scripts/ + references/
    productivity/nano-pdf/SKILL.md
    productivity/ocr-and-documents/SKILL.md + scripts/
    productivity/maps/SKILL.md + scripts/
    research/arxiv/SKILL.md + scripts/
    research/blogwatcher/SKILL.md
    media/youtube-content/SKILL.md + scripts/

GJ も同一構成を維持:
  - category 階層 (productivity/ research/ media/) を保持
  - SKILL.md を 1 行も改変しない (forkしない)
  - gj-skills/ に flat コピーしない
  - scripts/ references/ をそのまま使う
```

### 採用方法: vendor tree をそのまま参照 (コピー・改変ゼロ)

これら 7 種は **無改変の公式 skill**。最大限の整合 = **vendor の元ファイルをその場で使う**。

```
vendor/hermes-agent/skills/{category}/{name}/   ← 既に submodule で存在
    ↓ Dockerfile: COPY hermes-agent/ /app/hermes-agent/  (既存、skills/ 全体が入る)
/app/hermes-agent/skills/{category}/{name}/     ← container 内に公式構成のまま配置済
```

**gj-skills/ にコピーしない。** google-workspace は OAuth の AgentCore 特殊事情で fork したが、
この 7 種は OAuth 不要・改変不要 → 公式ファイルをそのまま参照する。

---

## 現状ギャップ: official-skills external_dir が解決されていない

### 問題

`entrypoint.sh:739` は `external_dirs: [official-skills, /opt/gj-skills]` を書くが、
`skill_utils.py:308` で相対パスは **HERMES_HOME 基準**で解決される:

```python
# 相対パスは HERMES_HOME (/mnt/workspace/.hermes) 基準
if not p.is_absolute():
    p = (hermes_home / p).resolve()   # → /mnt/workspace/.hermes/official-skills
```

→ `official-skills` = `/mnt/workspace/.hermes/official-skills`
→ **このディレクトリは作成されていない** → 公式 skill は現状 index に出ていない (silently skip、`skill_utils.py:320`)

### 修正: 公式 skill tree を絶対パスで external_dir に追加

**ファイル:** `gj-hermes-agent-core/docker/entrypoint.sh:739`

```python
# Before
f.write('\nskills:\n  external_dirs:\n    - official-skills\n    - /opt/gj-skills\n')

# After: 公式 skills tree を絶対パスで指定 (公式フォルダ構成のまま公開)
f.write('\nskills:\n  external_dirs:\n'
        '    - /app/hermes-agent/skills\n'   # 公式 skills tree 全体 (構成そのまま)
        '    - /opt/gj-skills\n')
```

→ `/app/hermes-agent/skills/productivity/powerpoint/` 等が公式パスのまま index に出る。

> ⚠️ 注意: これで公式 90 skill 全部が index に出る。不要 skill (apple/gaming 等) を除外したい場合は
> `requires_toolsets` frontmatter (issue #109) で自然にフィルタされる (該当 tool 無効なら非表示)。
> または採用 7 種だけを別ディレクトリに symlink する案も可 (構成は維持)。下記「絞り込み」参照。

### 絞り込み案 (7種だけ出したい場合、構成維持)

```bash
# entrypoint.sh: 採用 skill だけを公式構成のまま symlink
mkdir -p /mnt/workspace/.hermes/adopted-skills/productivity
ln -s /app/hermes-agent/skills/productivity/powerpoint  /mnt/workspace/.hermes/adopted-skills/productivity/
ln -s /app/hermes-agent/skills/productivity/nano-pdf     /mnt/workspace/.hermes/adopted-skills/productivity/
# ... category 階層を保ったまま symlink
# external_dirs に /mnt/workspace/.hermes/adopted-skills を追加
```

symlink でも **公式の category/name 構成は完全保持**される。

---

## 実行基盤: 各 skill の runtime 依存

skill の scripts/ は terminal/execute_code toolset (公式実行経路) で subprocess 実行される。
**依存を Dockerfile に bake する。**

| skill | 依存 (Dockerfile に追加) |
|-------|------------------------|
| powerpoint | `pip: markitdown[pptx] Pillow openpyxl` / `npm: pptxgenjs` / `apt: libreoffice` (soffice) |
| nano-pdf | nano-pdf CLI (`pip install nano-pdf` 等、SKILL.md 記載の入手法) |
| ocr-and-documents | `pip: pymupdf pymupdf4llm` (+ marker-pdf は任意) |
| maps | なし (OSM/OSRM ネットワークのみ、`requires_toolsets: [terminal]`) |
| arxiv | なし (純 Python + ネットワーク) |
| blogwatcher | blogwatcher-cli (Go バイナリ、`JulienTant/blogwatcher-cli`) |
| youtube-content | `pip: youtube-transcript-api` 等 (SKILL.md 記載) |

**ファイル:** `gj-hermes-agent-core/docker/Dockerfile`

```dockerfile
# 公式 skill 7種の runtime 依存 (issue #111)
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        libreoffice-impress libreoffice-core \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir \
        "markitdown[pptx]" pymupdf pymupdf4llm youtube-transcript-api nano-pdf
RUN npm install -g pptxgenjs
# blogwatcher-cli は release バイナリを curl で取得
RUN curl -fsSL <blogwatcher release url> -o /usr/local/bin/blogwatcher-cli && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/blogwatcher-cli
```

> 依存が重い (LibreOffice ~400MB)。image サイズ増を許容するか、powerpoint を後回しにするか要判断。

---

## 実行 toolset の確認

skill scripts は terminal / execute_code toolset で動く。GJ で当該 toolset が有効か確認:
- 有効 → そのまま動く (公式経路)
- 無効/サンドボックス制約 → google_api_mcp.py 同様の MCP wrapper が必要 (ただし wrapper は mcp_servers/ に置き、SKILL.md 構成は公式のまま維持)

---

## 実装タスク

- [ ] `entrypoint.sh`: external_dirs を `/app/hermes-agent/skills` (絶対パス) に修正、または採用7種を公式構成で symlink
- [ ] `Dockerfile`: 7 skill の runtime 依存を bake (libreoffice / pip / npm / blogwatcher-cli)
- [ ] 実行 toolset (terminal/execute_code) が AgentCore で動くか検証。不可なら MCP wrapper 検討 (SKILL.md は公式構成維持)
- [ ] **公式 SKILL.md を 1 行も改変しないことを確認** (gj-skills/ にコピーしない)
- [ ] Runtime deploy → ChatWork 経由で各 skill を 1 つずつ E2E テスト:
  - [ ] arxiv: 「機械学習の最新論文を探して」
  - [ ] youtube-content: YouTube URL → 要約
  - [ ] maps: 「東京駅から渋谷駅の経路」
  - [ ] ocr: PDF 添付 → 文字抽出
  - [ ] nano-pdf: PDF 誤字修正
  - [ ] blogwatcher: RSS 監視登録
  - [ ] powerpoint: 「提案資料を pptx で作って」
- [ ] `docs/gj/current/agent/ADOPTED_SKILLS_common.md`: 採用 skill 一覧 + 公式パス + 依存を記録

---

## やらないこと (スコープ外・原則)

- **公式 SKILL.md / scripts/ の改変** (無改変でそのまま使う)
- **gj-skills/ への flat コピー** (公式 category 構成を壊さない)
- 7 種以外の skill 採用 (別 issue)

---

## 参考

- 公式 skills: `vendor/hermes-agent/skills/{productivity,research,media}/`
- external_dir 解決: `vendor/hermes-agent/agent/skill_utils.py:241,300-320` (相対=HERMES_HOME基準)
- GJ skill 設定: `gj-hermes-agent-core/docker/entrypoint.sh:739`
- skill 実行前例: `mcp_servers/google_api_mcp.py` `run_skill_script()`
- 関連: issue #109 (requires_tools 整備), #110 (Progressive Disclosure), #65 (提案スライド)

items.body:
## Bug Description

When running a one-shot CLI chat with an explicit provider override for a named custom provider, the main response succeeds, but auxiliary title generation still appears to use the default main model (`gpt-5.5`) and fails with a user-visible warning.

This happened with a local Ollama-backed provider configured as an OpenAI-compatible custom provider.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a named custom provider that points to an Ollama OpenAI-compatible endpoint:

```yaml
model:
  default: gpt-5.5
  provider: openai-codex
  api_mode: chat_completions

providers:
  ollama-local:
    name: Ollama Local
    base_url: http://localhost:11434/v1
    api_key: no-key-required
    api_mode: chat_completions
    model: qwen3.6:35b-mlx
    default_model: qwen3.6:35b-mlx
    models:
      qwen3.6:35b-mlx:
        context_length: 262144
```

2. Confirm the Ollama OpenAI-compatible API works:

```bash
curl http://localhost:11434/v1/models
```

3. Run Hermes with the provider override:

```bash
hermes chat -q "Introduce yourself in one sentence." --provider ollama-local
```

## Expected Behavior

The explicit CLI provider override should apply consistently to the one-shot session, including auxiliary title generation, or auxiliary title generation should gracefully skip/fail silently if it cannot use the selected provider.

At minimum, a successful main response should not end with a user-visible warning caused by an unrelated auxiliary task.

## Actual Behavior

The main response succeeds using the local Ollama provider, but the command ends with:

```text
⚠ Auxiliary title generation failed: HTTP 404: model 'gpt-5.5' not found
```

Example output:

```text
Query: Introduce yourself in one sentence.
Initializing agent...
────────────────────────────────────────

╭─ ⚕ Hermes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
    Hello, I am a local Hermes assistant running through an Ollama-backed provider.
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

Resume this session with:
  hermes --resume <session_id>

Session:        <session_id>
Duration:       35s
Messages:       2 (1 user, 0 tool calls)
⚠ Auxiliary title generation failed: HTTP 404: model 'gpt-5.5' not found
```

## Why This Looks Like a Bug

The command explicitly requested:

```bash
--provider ollama-local
```

The configured provider has its own model:

```yaml
model: qwen3.6:35b-mlx
default_model: qwen3.6:35b-mlx
```

The main chat path honors the override and returns a valid response, but the auxiliary title generation path appears to still resolve to the global default model (`gpt-5.5`). In an Ollama/OpenAI-compatible local endpoint, that model is not available, so the auxiliary request returns 404.

## Related Issues

This appears related to existing auxiliary/title-generation behavior issues, but I could not find an exact match for CLI `--provider` override + named custom Ollama provider + `gpt-5.5` 404:

- #23246 — gateway should keep auto-title generation failures silent
- #32729 — auxiliary title generation timeout config is ignored
- #21566 — auxiliary calls use short defaults / local endpoint handling
- #17413 — auxiliary provider:auto selected a broken fallback provider instead of main provider

## Proposed Fix

Possible fixes:

1. When `hermes chat --provider <provider>` is used, propagate the effective provider/model into auxiliary title generation for that session.
2. If the auxiliary task is configured as `provider: auto`, prefer the session's effective provider/model before falling back to global defaults.
3. If title generation fails after the main response succeeds, avoid surfacing it as a user-visible warning in CLI unless verbose/debug mode is enabled.
4. Optionally add a config option to disable title generation or make auxiliary failures silent for successful one-shot CLI runs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `hermes chat -q "..." --provider ollama-local` succeeds without attempting title generation against `gpt-5.5` unless explicitly configured to do so.
- Named custom providers with `model` / `default_model` are respected by auxiliary title generation when selected via CLI provider override.
- Auxiliary title generation failure does not make a successful main response look partially failed to the user.
- Regression test covers CLI provider override with a named custom provider and auxiliary title generation enabled.
