items.body:
## Summary

When you switch models mid-session via Telegram (e.g. from grok-4.3 to openrouter/owl-alpha), the main conversation uses the new model correctly. But any auxiliary call triggered by a real tool call can silently route through a completely different, **paid** model on **OpenRouter** using stale Codex OAuth credentials — costing you real money.

I got charged ~$1 US for a single GPT-5.5 call I never authorised, at 3:44pm AEST on 1 June 2026. Not because I configured it. Not because I selected it. Because Hermes' internal routing decided to use it when my actual selected model (owl-alpha, free) had a transient issue during a tool call.

## Reproduction steps

1. Have `openai-codex` credentials in your auth pool (any OAuth login).
2. Have `model.default: grok-4.3` on disk but switch session-level to `openrouter/owl-alpha` mid-conversation.
3. Run a tool-heavy workflow (portfolio refinement, website audit, anything with multiple tool calls).
4. Watch the log for an unauthorised paid auxiliary call that routes via OpenRouter/Codex pool, not your fallback chain.

## Expected behaviour

The fallback chain should **only** reference models the user explicitly authorised — via the session-level model, on-disk `fallback_providers`, or `auxiliary.*` sections. The credential pool should not be an implicit fallback target for paid routing unless the user has actively selected that provider.

If the session-level model (owl-alpha) fails, the fallback should exhaust the user's declared free fallback chain (owl-alpha → gpt-120b:free → deepseek-v4-flash:free) before even considering any other provider. It should **never** silently bill a model the user never selected.

## Current fix is insufficient

Existing issue #24029 and PR #25316 only append `:free` to the hardcoded auxiliary model if your main model already ends in `:free`. This does nothing for:
- Users on free models without the `:free` suffix (openrouter/owl-alpha)
- Users who switch models mid-session (the model switch doesn't propagate to auxiliary paths)
- Users who have Codex/Nvidia/other paid providers in the credential pool but don't want them used as fallback targets

## Root cause as I understand it

- `auxiliary_client.py` has hardcoded OpenRouter fallback constants (`_OPENROUTER_MODEL`, `_NOUS_MODEL`) that don't respect the session's active model
- The credential pool (`auth.json`) is treated as an eligible fallback source regardless of which provider the user is currently using
- Session-level model switches (Telegram `/model`) only affect the main conversation loop — auxiliary paths and fallback routing continue reading stale on-disk config
- `auxiliary.vision` and other sub-paths that are set to the old provider (e.g. xai-oauth/grok-4.3) become leak paths when the old provider is unavailable

## The bits I'd actually like fixed

1. Session-level model switches should pin the entire fallback chain to only the user's selected provider and fallbacks
2. The credential pool should **not** be an implicit fallback target — if I have Codex OAuth but have selected owl-alpha, Codex should never be routed to unless I explicitly switch to it
3. There should be some audit trail — the user should be able to see *why* a particular model was selected when the billing spike hits, not have to grep source code and config files to reconstruct the route
4. The `auxiliary_client.py` defaults should be genuinely free models (meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free) rather than paid Vertex/Gemini models that bill users who never configured them

## System info

- Hermes version: whatever was current 1 June 2026
- Profile: claudia (gateway/Telegram session)
- Active model at time of issue: openrouter/owl-alpha
- Fallback chain: owl-alpha → gpt-120b:free → deepseek-v4-flash:free
- Actual model billed: GPT-5.5 via OpenRouter at ~$1 AUD
- How I found it: checked my OpenRouter usage dashboard at openrouter.ai/account/usage — the call was logged there against a model I never selected. No local log entry or notification alerted me.

items.title: [RFC] Treat "context selection/routing" as a first-class ContextEngine concern, distinct from compression

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## TL;DR

The `ContextEngine` ABC is shaped entirely around **compression** — shrinking an over-budget transcript. But a growing number of third-party engines aren't trying to compress; they want to **select or replace** which context goes into each turn (retrieval, topic routing, role switching). Today the only way to do that is to force `should_compress()` to always return `True` and abuse `compress()` as a per-turn callback. That backdoor is the shared root cause behind a cluster of open issues, and it actively degrades UX when the engine's backend is unavailable.

This RFC asks whether Hermes would consider treating **context selection** as a first-class ContextEngine concern, parallel to compression — e.g. an optional, no-op-by-default `select_context()` hook called every turn before generation. I'm not asking for a specific implementation; I'm asking whether the direction is one the maintainers would welcome a PR toward.

---

## 1. Where this is coming from (so you can calibrate)

I'll be upfront: I'm building an early-stage context engine of my own, so I have skin in this game. But the reason I'm writing a discussion rather than just a PR for my own use case is that, while researching how to solve my problem, I found that **a lot of people have independently hit the same wall** — and they're all working around it in the same way. This looks like an architectural gap, not five separate feature requests. I'd rather surface the pattern than add a sixth patch.

I've read the relevant parts of the current source (`agent/context_engine.py`, `agent/conversation_loop.py`, `hermes_cli/plugins.py`) to make sure the problem description below is accurate to `main`, not to my assumptions.

---

## 2. The pattern: compression is the only first-class verb

`ContextEngine`'s lifecycle has exactly one load-bearing path for touching the message list:

```
update_from_response() → should_compress() → compress(messages, ...)
```

`compress()` is the **only** hook that receives the full message list with the intent of changing it, and it only fires when `should_compress()` returns `True` (i.e. near the token limit). The ABC docstring states this plainly: a context engine "controls how conversation context is managed **when approaching the model's token limit**."

That assumption — *engines only act when the context is nearly full* — is correct for compression. It does not hold for an engine whose job is to decide, **every turn**, *which* context is relevant in the first place.

---

## 3. Everyone hitting this is working around it the same way

Engines that need per-turn access to the message list are forced to make `should_compress()` lie:

```python
def should_compress(self, prompt_tokens=0) -> bool:
    return True  # not a budget decision — I just need compress() called every turn
```

This isn't hypothetical. The same workaround (or a request to remove the need for it) shows up independently across at least five projects:

- **#23837** (hermes-mneme, retrieval): explicitly titled "currently requires abusing compress() as a backdoor."
- **#24949** (lossless-hermes): proposes a `preassemble()` hook because `should_compress=True` every turn rotates the SQLite session ID and breaks lineage.
- **#15498** (SPC-ctx): proposes `ingest_message()` + `after_turn()` hooks for per-turn tightening that `compress()` can't express.
- **#23892**: proposes host-managed async compression preparation, again because the single synchronous `compress()` path is too blunt.
- **#25115** (hermes-lcm): the same architectural smell surfacing in the UI — the host shows "📦 Preflight compression…" even when the active engine isn't compressing.

Related: **#22929**, **#16501**, **#29370**, **#20316** all circle the same area.

Each of these is reasonable on its own. But taken together they read less like five feature requests and more like one missing abstraction being patched five different ways.

---

## 4. The workaround actively hurts users (not just cosmetics)

Beyond inflated `compression_count` and misleading HUD text (#25115), the `should_compress=True` backdoor has a correctness cost.

In my own dogfooding, my engine talks to a local backend. When that backend is unreachable, the honest behavior is to do nothing and let Hermes fall back to its built-in compressor. But because `should_compress()` is hardwired to `True`, the host proceeds as if compression is warranted, and the built-in compressor engages at its default threshold — on a large-context model, that's aggressive compaction of a session nowhere near its budget. The net effect: **installing the engine and having its backend go down is worse than not installing it at all.** (This looks related to #29370.)

I had to special-case `should_compress()` to return `False` when the backend is down just to recover a "no worse than default" guarantee. That's a symptom of the abstraction, not of my code.

---

## 5. The underlying gap: selection ≠ compression

The whole ecosystem conversation right now is about *how to compress better* — lossless DAGs, summary stubs, async preparation, gradual tightening. That's valuable. But it's all the same verb: take an over-long context and make it shorter.

There's a second verb that the ABC has no vocabulary for: **selecting or replacing which context is relevant for this turn, before generation, regardless of whether the context is full.** Retrieval engines do it. Topic-routing engines do it. Role-switching and conversation-branching engines do it. They don't want to shrink the existing context; they want to *choose a different one*.

Naming it makes it tractable. Compression and selection are orthogonal:

- **Compression**: context is too long → make it shorter. (Today's `compress()`.)
- **Selection / routing**: this turn belongs to a different context → use that one. (No hook today.)

An engine can want one, the other, or both.

---

## 6. What I'm actually asking for

Not a specific API — a direction. Concretely, the shape that would resolve the pattern is an optional, no-op-by-default hook called every turn before the model request, allowed to return the message list to use for that turn:

```python
def select_context(
    self,
    messages: List[Dict[str, Any]],
    *,
    incoming_message: Dict[str, Any] = None,
    budget_tokens: int = 0,
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]] | None:
    """Optional. Choose/replace the context for THIS turn, before generation.
    Return the message list to use, or None to fall through unchanged.
    Default: return None (no-op). Not a compression decision."""
    return None
```

(Name negotiable — `select_context`, `route_context`, `assemble_context`, whatever fits Hermes conventions.) The key properties that matter:

- Fires **every turn before generation**, independent of `should_compress()`.
- May **replace** the message list, not only append (this is what distinguishes it from the existing `pre_llm_call` plugin hook, which appends to the user message and intentionally never rewrites the list to preserve the cache prefix).
- **Optional, no-op default** — zero impact on the built-in compressor or any existing engine.

I'm not attached to the signature. I'm asking whether "selection as a first-class concern" is a direction worth a PR.

---

## 7. Why this is worth it for Hermes (not just for plugin authors)

**1. It collapses a cluster of patches into one clean concept.** Instead of landing `preassemble` + `ingest_message` + `after_turn` + async-prepare hooks separately — each solving one project's slice — a selection hook addresses the shared root cause. Fewer overlapping APIs to maintain.

**2. It removes a class of bugs at the source.** Every engine currently forced to return `should_compress=True` is a latent source of the inflated-counter, misleading-status, and backend-down-degradation issues. Give them an honest hook and `should_compress()` goes back to meaning what it says.

**3. It opens a plugin category Hermes doesn't serve yet.** Retrieval-augmented, topic-routed, role-aware, and branchable context engines are a natural growth area for an agent framework. Right now the ABC quietly excludes all of them by only speaking "compression." Supporting selection is how that category becomes first-class.

**4. The strategic one.** The whole field is converging on "how do we compress context better." Comparatively little attention goes to "how do we choose the right context in the first place." If Hermes acknowledges selection/routing as a distinct, supported concern at the architecture level, it's taking a position the rest of the field hasn't — that managing context is not the same as compressing it. That's a small change in surface area and a meaningful one in stance.

---

## 8. Non-goals (keeping this small)

- **No change** to `should_compress()` / `compress()` / `update_from_response()` semantics. This is purely additive.
- **No forced migration.** The hook is optional with a no-op default; the built-in `ContextCompressor` and every existing engine are untouched.
- **Not the plugin-loading discussion.** Discovery/registration paths are a separate topic; out of scope here.
- **Not asking for an immediate implementation.** If the direction is welcome, I'm happy to draft a PR and align on the signature first.

---

## 9. A concrete reference, offered with full disclosure

If a real example is useful, my own engine — [Doctor Chaos](https://github.com/doctorchaos-ai/doctor-chaos), which routes each message to a "topic space" and uses that space's history as the turn's context — is the purest "selection, not compression" case I know of, which is why I ended up writing this. **Full disclosure: it's early-stage and I'm obviously an interested party, so please treat it as one data point, not a motivation for the proposal.** The proposal stands on the pattern across the issues above, not on my project. I'm offering the repo only in case a concrete "this is what a pure selection engine looks like" reference helps the discussion.

Happy to be wrong about any of this — if there's an existing path I've missed that lets an engine replace per-turn context without the `should_compress=True` workaround, I'd genuinely like to know.

items.title: MCP OAuth: no auto-recovery from invalid_client / 'Redirect URI Mismatch' on stale dynamic client registration
items.body:
## Summary

When an MCP server's dynamically-registered OAuth client (`~/.hermes/mcp-tokens/<server>.client.json`) becomes invalid server-side (e.g. IdP redeploy, DB migration, rebrand), Hermes continues to present the dead `client_id` indefinitely. The IdP rejects it with **'Redirect URI Mismatch'** (underlying error: `invalid_client`), and Hermes does not detect this condition or re-run dynamic client registration. The user has to manually delete the three cache files (`<server>.json`, `<server>.client.json`, `<server>.meta.json`) for each affected server and re-run `hermes mcp test`.

This has happened three times in two weeks for me on the Wix mcp-s/Willow stack (github, jira, excalidraw), all sharing the same IdP at `https://mcp-s-connect.wewix.net/`.

## Reproduction

1. Configure any `auth: oauth` MCP server in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`.
2. Complete OAuth flow once — tokens cached, all good.
3. Wait for the IdP to redeploy / migrate / wipe dynamic client registrations server-side. (For mcp-s/Willow this happens unpredictably every couple of weeks.)
4. Run `hermes mcp test <server>` or start Hermes → browser opens with the cached `client_id` URL → consent page shows **'Redirect URI Mismatch — The redirect URI does not match any registered URI for this client'**.
5. Hermes prints a connect timeout. Retrying does NOT help; the cached client is permanently dead.

## Evidence that tokens are not the problem

Inspecting `~/.hermes/mcp-tokens/github.json` shows `expires_in: 86400000` (~2.7 years) and `expires_at` ~2029. Refresh tokens are also valid. The breakage is purely the registered client, not the credentials it holds.

## Expected behavior

When the authorization endpoint or token endpoint returns `invalid_client` (or the IdP's UI returns a redirect mismatch despite our redirect_uri being correctly derived from `client.json`), Hermes should:

1. Treat the cached `<server>.client.json` + `<server>.meta.json` as poisoned.
2. Delete them (with a small backup).
3. Re-run RFC 7591 dynamic client registration against `registration_endpoint` from a freshly fetched discovery doc.
4. Retry the OAuth flow with the new `client_id`.

This would turn a recurring 3-step manual ritual into invisible self-healing.

## Workaround

Until then, I wrote a small reset script (`hermes-mcp-reset`) that auto-discovers `auth: oauth` servers from `config.yaml`, backs up tokens, wipes the stale files, and re-auths sequentially. Happy to PR something similar as a built-in `hermes mcp reauth --all` subcommand if useful.

## Secondary observation: startup popup storm

When multiple OAuth servers are simultaneously stale at startup, Hermes opens N browser tabs at once, each with its own ~40s callback listener. A human can only complete one OAuth flow at a time → the others time out and stay broken. Two possible mitigations: (a) serialize OAuth flows at startup, only one at a time; (b) defer OAuth dance until the tool is first invoked rather than at startup. Either would be a UX improvement.

## Environment

- Hermes: latest as of 2026-06-01
- macOS 26.4
- MCP servers affected: `auth: oauth` HTTP transport against mcp-s.wewix.net / Willow IdP
- Stdio MCP-S servers (`USER_ACCESS_KEY` env) are unaffected — this is purely a dynamic-client-registration issue.

items.body:
Adds native stepfun STT provider to tools/transcription_tools.py, supporting StepFun's StepAudio 2.5 ASR API via POST /v1/audio/asr/sse.
    
    What
    
    - New provider branch in _get_provider() — activates when stt.provider: stepfun is set in config.yaml and STEPFUN_API_KEY is available.
    - New _transcribe_stepfun() implementation using stdlib urllib + SSE streaming parser (no new dependencies).
    - New dispatcher branch in transcribe_audio() with configurable model default (stepaudio-2.5-asr).
    - New _encode_audio_base64() helper.
    
    Config
    
    yaml
    stt:
      provider: stepfun
      stepfun:
        model: stepaudio-2.5-asr
        language: ko   # optional, defaults to ko
    
    
    Environment: STEPFUN_API_KEY (required), STEPFUN_BASE_URL (optional, defaults to https://api.stepfun.ai/v1).
    
    Design decisions
    
    - Follows existing provider pattern: mirrors _transcribe_xai / _transcribe_openai structure — env check in _get_provider(), dedicated transcribe* function, dispatcher branch with model fallback.
    - No new dependencies: uses stdlib urllib, json, base64 only.
    - URL safety: if STEPFUN_BASE_URL contains step_plan, it's rewritten to /v1 before calling /audio/asr/sse (audio endpoints return 404 under /step_plan/v1).
    - Format inference: .ogg → ogg/opus, all other supported formats → mp3/mp3.
    - Language resolution: stt.stepfun.language → HERMES_LOCAL_STT_LANGUAGE env var → "ko".
    - Credential resolution: uses get_env_value() (not os.getenv()) so keys in ~/.hermes/.env are found correctly.
    
    Testing
    
    - Existing tests/tools/test_transcription_tools.py: 95/95 passed — no regressions.
    - Discord voice end-to-end test: transcription works correctly with stt.provider: stepfun in production config.
    
    Notes
    
    - This is a additive change — no existing providers or code paths were modified.
    - StepFun is not included in the auto-detect fallback chain; users must set stt.provider: stepfun explicitly.
